title: Three consecutive commuting squares give an arrow isomorphism
statement: In any category, let a,b,c and d,e,f be three composable arrows. If four vertex isomorphisms make the three corresponding squares commute, then the composites a followed by b followed by c and d followed by e followed by f are isomorphic as objects of the arrow category.

proof.text: Reassociate compositions and substitute the third, second, and first commuting-square equations. The resulting equality says the endpoint isomorphisms commute with the composite arrows. Apply Arrow.isoMk. The factored-comparison variant carries the specified total arrows as parameters and their three-factor equations as fields; substitution gives the same arrow comparison without unfolding the total functors.
